The naming layer lives only in bordercall, and every result is on synthetic spines.

**Exact rule.** schwingcheck/rule.py is the exact Bayes rule over Panjabi's tables. It names typical columns from C3 to L5.

**Chain of levels.** schwingcheck/chain.py (PRs 20, 23, 31; records/chain-2026-10-28/) adds six-lumbar and T13 columns and missed bodies. With all 32 measures it names:

| Column | 3 bodies | 5 bodies | 9 bodies |
|---|---|---|---|
| Typical | 96.0% | 98.0% | 99.0% |
| Six-lumbar | 97.5% | 98.5% | 98.0% |
| T13 | 94.5% | 98.0% | 97.5% |

At 0.99 it is right on at least 99.37% of answers. Medians are 2.39, 6.6 and 78.6 ms at 3, 5 and 9 bodies, on one CPU. There is no p95 and no ONNX parity.

**Budget.** 97 ms is one frame of C-ArmLSpine's 10.3 fps sweeps, and the p95 must be under it (SchwingNet docs/memory/latency-and-the-recorded-sweep.md).

**JAX layer.** autoanatomist/naming.py (PR 27) adds four_lumbar, anchors and a per-value error, and matches chain.py exactly.

**One body.** A lone typical body is named 86.8% of the time. A lone L6 is named 12.6%, and every one of its 0.99 answers is wrong (PR 32).

**Input it needs.** Per-body values for any of the 32 measures in mm, mm² or degrees, ordered top to bottom, NaN where missing, each with its error.

facts.fact: The exact rule is SchwingCheck: an exact Bayes rule over Panjabi's tables. It covers typical C3 to L5 (22 levels, 23 - n places) with a uniform prior. The likelihood per measure is rank-one plus diagonal (rho 0.5, sigma_err 1 mm). Size log s ~ N(0, 0.07^2) is integrated by 161-node Gauss-Hermite or a 281-node trapezoid. Gaps and missing values are handled.
The pool holds 32 measures: 18 lengths, 6 areas and 8 angles. Errors are 1 mm, sqrt(pi A/2) mm^2 and 3 degrees. The owner chose to keep all 32 as printed at 2026-10-29 09:01 UTC.
With the seven SPINEPS measures on typical columns, the exact rule names exactly 47.3/73.1/85.7/96.1/99.7% of fields at 1/3/5/9/15 bodies, and is right 99.70 to 99.98% of the time at 0.99.
Build-up at 3 bodies, typical columns: 1 measure 42.0%, the seven 73.1%, the first seven chosen greedily 89.2%, all 32 98.3%.

Anomalous columns at 3/5/9 bodies with all 32 measures: six lumbar 93.7/94.5/93.3%, T13 92.6/91.9/92.8%, four lumbar 98.2/99.8/100%, rib on L1 97.4/99.7/100%, no rib on T12 97.1/99.7/100%. With the seven: six lumbar 70.3/81.1/89.3%, T13 69.1/77.3/87.2%. With all 32, 5.1 to 7.2% of 0.99 answers on L6/T13 spines are wrong.

Chain of levels with all 32 measures, share named exactly at 1/3/5/9 bodies: typical 86.5/96.0/98.0/99.0% (the consecutive rule gives 88.5/88.0/72.5 at 3/5/9); six lumbar 85.0/97.5/98.5/98.0%; T13 84.0/94.5/98.0/97.5%. At 0.99 the chain is right on at least 99.37% of every type at 3 to 9 bodies, while the consecutive rule falls as low as 72.11%.

Chain speed, built once, all 32 measures, one machine's medians: 1.28/2.39/6.6/21.3/78.6 ms at 1/3/5/7/9 bodies, over 24/92/339/1,166/3,896 paths. With the seven: 0.267 to 23.1 ms. path_logev takes 11.8 ms to 16.4 s. No p95, no device port.

rule.py speed on the trapezoid, one thread, 3 bodies: 0.31 ms (1 measure), 1.12 ms (7), 4.02 ms (16), 9.68 ms (32). NUTS takes 166 to 712 times as long. At 16 measures NUTS was once 1.0 wrong at R-hat 1.00.
The 97 ms budget is one frame of C-ArmLSpine's 10.3 fps sweeps. Real time means p95 strictly under it, on a runtime whose ONNX parity passed for the same file.
Data axis: tables re-estimated from 12 people break the 0.99 promise (97.99% for typical columns at 5 bodies with all 32). From 50 people they hold at least 99.34%.

One vertebra, all 32 measures: a lone typical body is named exactly 86.8% of the time and within one level 96.9%. It is answered at 0.99 42.1% of the time and right 99.85%. With the seven it is named 46.2%. A lone L6 is named 12.6% and a lone T13 47.4%, and every one of their 0.99 answers is wrong. T4 to T7 are named 63.4 to 67.2%. Below C7 is decided on 99.8% of bodies and below T12 on 99.3%.

The JAX naming layer adds a four_lumbar type (weight 0.05), top/bottom anchors and a per-value error, and uses soft-Viterbi. It is exact against chain.py within 1e-9 to 1e-13. Enumeration memory in float32 is 1.2 MB at 3 bodies, 7.6 MB at 5, 77 MB at 8 and 1.15 GB at 12.

The input the naming layer needs from a frame pipeline: an ordered top-to-bottom list of bodies, each with values for any subset of the 32 measures in their units (lengths in mm, areas in mm^2, angles in degrees), NaN where missing, a per-value error, optional gaps or offsets, and optional top/bottom anchors.

The real-time frame model, its latency,.area: The real-time frame model, its latency, and the demo video on an MP4 of a fluoroscopic spine pan
The real-time frame model, its latency,.summary:
SchwingNet's version 1 is only a level stage. It is a ResNet-18 with a 27-way head (C1 to sacrum, T13 and L6 included) that reads 64 px crops cut from truth boxes. It needs no segmentation at inference, but it does need a box for every vertebra, and no detector has been built (docs/research/v1-demo/DEVIATIONS.md item 4).

For each box it gives a level and its probability. A causal IoU tracker smooths these and shows "?" below 0.5 (src/schwingnet/sweep.py).

On real frames it has run once: e4f7054848f5, grid job 40702198, 21 of 21 test crops from 4 persons. The PREREG frozen today in #464 treats that result as calibration only. The run is not recorded in the repository (#256), and the evaluation page shows only the two synthetic dry runs.

The reported stack in spine-program 01 also works without masks at inference: YOLO detectors, the encoder and a BiGRU head. On C-ArmLSpine it names 595 of 617 lateral bodies (96.4 %, 141 cases) and 276 of 631 AP bodies (43.7 %). Its truth comes from two machines counting from the sacrum. No human read it, and no C2 is in the field.

Latency has been measured only in the synthetic dry run: ONNX Runtime on 4 CPU threads, p50 9.4 ms and p95 15.1 ms, with parity passed. The three v1 latency jobs, 40702515 to 40702517, pended for more than 60 hours. They dropped off the status page on 2026-10-25, and what became of them is not recorded (#138).

The 97 ms budget is 1000 / 10.3 fps (src/schwingnet/latency.py; the 10.3 fps comes from spine-program CINE_DEMO_RECON line 187).

tools/sweep.py writes an overlay MP4 (or a GIF when ffmpeg is missing). It reads only PNG folders or .npy stacks, plus one line of boxes per frame. There is no MP4 reader, and the budget stays at 97 ms whatever the frame rate.

case134 and case39 are rotational CBCT spins, not pans. case134 has projected SPINEPS boxes but no level truth, and case39 has no export. The only real panning MP4s on the grid are the four Bern myelography clips (7.5 fps, CC BY, truth from the captions only).

Four gate words still submit plain Slurm jobs: latency, experiment, bench and anomaly timing (flows/README.md). The LatencyFlow work in progress (5407bef) is not on origin.

The demo still lacks:
- a detector
- LatencyFlow
- an MP4 reader with a budget set by each file's frame rate
- naming that follows a pan across frames
- a clip with truth
- the V1Flow run
- latency measured with ONNX parity on the H200
- the owner's choices

facts.fact: At inference v1 reads only an 8-bit frame and boxes (crop, forward pass, softmax, tracker step). No mask is read. The prior=level-map block is a training-only head, and best.pt and every reader are unchanged.

Per frame v1 outputs each box's level and probability, smoothed by a causal tracker: greedy IoU at least 0.3, a moving average with weight 0.5 on the new frame, a track ending after 3 unseen frames, and '?' when the best level is under 0.5. sweep.jsonl records boxes, tracks, levels, probabilities and timing.

The one v1 run on real frames is e4f7054848f5 (grid job 40702198, 5 min 16 s on one GPU, commit 8116aae, catalog 1 252ba19562cf): 21 of 21 test crops from 4 persons, a Wilson interval of about 0.85 to 1. It exists only on the grid.

The frozen v1 PREREG treats e4f7054848f5's 21/21 as calibration, never a result. It pre-registers a new run on catalog sha256 94c79afd..., 20 epochs, seed 1, crops of 64 px, ImageNet resnet18-f37072fd.pth, as an estimate with no accuracy bar. The 97 ms bar is left to 'the latency word's, under a pre-registration of its own'.
The evaluation page holds only the two synthetic dry runs (a767a466f5c1, cd37124c487d), with latency 'not measured' for both.

The reported stack has no segmentation at inference: naming detector detector_v5z_final (YOLO11m-pose, 4 corner keypoints), sacrum and vertebra detector rx_lodo_carmlspine_1024 (YOLO11m), the allspine_v9 encoder (ResNet-18, two-channel stem of image plus target marker, 27 classes), a BiGRU head, the count from the sacrum and the alphabet coupling. Per vertebra it outputs a level, a probability, an entropy and an abstain flag.

The reported stack's accuracy on C-ArmLSpine, a C-arm it never saw: lateral 595/617 = 96.4 % [92.3, 98.4] over 141 cases; AP 276/631 = 43.7 %; fine-tuned five-fold lateral 97.4 %; detection recall at 0.74 231/287 = 80.5 %.

C-ArmLSpine level truth is TotalSegmentator and SPINEPS+VERIDAH agreeing on the CBCT, both counting from the sacrum: 814 of 910 vertebrae agree, and no level was set by a human. The test set is lumbar (T11 to sacrum), and no C2 anchor has been shown on a real intraoperative frame.

The 97 ms budget is one frame interval of C-ArmLSpine's sweeps, 1000 / 10.3 fps rounded down (BUDGET_MS = 97.0). The 10.3 fps comes from 301 frames over 29 s of acquisition time (case39 15:04:10 to 15:04:39, case134 15:12:31 to 15:13:00).

facts.fact: tools/sweep.py reads a sweep only as a folder of image files or an 8-bit .npy stack, plus a boxes.jsonl with one line per frame naming its frame. It refuses frames deeper than 8 bits. It writes overlay/*.png, sweep.jsonl, summary.json, contact.png, and sweep.mp4 through ffmpeg, or sweep.gif when ffmpeg is missing.
The sweep summary and overlay always use the 97 ms budget. --fps (default 10.3) sets only the video's frame rate and the GIF frame duration.
The overlay's corner text gives the frame counter, the gantry angle, this frame's compute time, the p95 so far against 97 ms, 'SchwingNet v1 <run id>', the runtime and device, and 'boxes: <source>'.

case134 export: 301 frames at 1024 x 1024, 8-bit, every frame with its meta (angle, mode, boxes, pose, ...), at /rs/rs_grp_oschome/go2432/data/realxray/carmlspine_sweep, readable by tools/sweep.py from-bank. case39 has no export, and its CBCT folder holds 696 files not yet told apart.

case134's truth is 4 SPINEPS body boxes per frame with level null, so it scores detection and tracking but not naming. Both sweeps are rotations from +122 to -52 degrees, not cranio-caudal pans. case134 and case39 are frozen test persons.
